governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral on the ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier: the strongest literature relationship (carotid sinus hypersensitivity present in 23 percent of unexplained recurrent fallers, with pacing reducing fall rates by two thirds, Kenny 2001; Richardson 1997) describes the cardioinhibitory response as the diagnostic finding of the syndrome itself and its symptomatic expression, so an edge to a syncope-family target would restate the diagnostic criterion as an empirical relationship.

Alternative-target check recorded: the catalog's only candidate targets are vasovagal-syncope (a distinct diagnostic entity with its own mechanism and workup, so mapping CSH into it would misclassify identity) and cardiac-arrhythmia (the sinus pauses are an expression of the same cardioinhibitory reflex finding); the clinically dominant downstream outcomes in the literature are falls and fall-related injury, which have no distinct catalog identity.

No edge was authored because a condition whose defining abnormality produces its presenting symptoms cannot support a legally meaningful secondary edge: the veteran's own standard (symptoms within the same diagnostic finding) is exactly the boundary this knowledge base enforces.
